transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-14 16:00 PT / Duration ~52m / Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Priya (Northbridge AE), Alex (Northbridge SE), Sarah (CedarBridge Head of Platform), Tom (CedarBridge CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i know we pushed this a week out so appreciate folks making time. quick roundtable, i'll kick off. i'm maya kapoor, ae on the redwood side.
[00:12] Priya: priya desai, northbridge, partner ae. excited to get cedarbridge over the finish line.
[00:18] Alex: alex kim, partner se at northbridge. i'll pair with jonah on any perf work.
[00:22] Sarah: sarah liu, head of platform at cedarbridge. looking forward to figuring throughput and the compliance bits.
[00:28] Tom: tom reyes, cto. i'll be high level but want to make sure procurement/ops are comfortable.
[00:33] Jonah: jonah price, redwood se. i'll own the performance bake and tech scoping.
[00:37] Lena: lena ortiz, csm, i'll be tracking deliverables and timelines.
[00:42] Maya: cool, agenda real quick: 1) align on cedarbridge success criteria 2) define perf/poC scope + dataset 3) partner economics + next steps 4) risk gating and exec path. any quick additions?
[00:52] Sarah: sounds good. one ask — we need to validate 99th pct latency at scale, not just p50.
[00:58] Maya: noted. we're doing that. okay we'll jump in.

[05:10] Jonah: quick context from redwood infra perspective — our serving runtime supports continuous batching and kv cache, we can do prefix caching for repeated prompts; often the delta is in sequence length distribution. in other words if cedarbridge has many short prompts we can batch more aggressively, if you have 4k token prompts that's a different path.
[05:36] Tom: right, our flows are mixed. Most API calls are ~200 tokens but we have episodic long runs for analytics summaries ~2K tokens.
[05:49] Priya: and i know cedarbridge cares about data residency — are you able to support a private deployment in region eu-west-1?
[05:58] Jonah: yes, we have private + vpc options. small caveat: dedicated capacity procurement lead time is longer, but for the perf bake we can simulate on hosted with region affinity.

[09:15] Alex: question — do you have any quantization / model recommendations for mixed workloads? we don't want cost to blow out for cedarbridge.
[09:24] Jonah: yes, we typically suggest a two-tier model profile: 1) a q4f quantized 8-bit variant for bulk queries, 2) a higher accuracy fp16 variant for the long episodic summaries. the routing can be policy driven so you get the best of both.

[12:00] Sarah: procurement timeline — we're targeting vendor selection by end of June, legal sign by mid-july. is that achievable?
[12:09] Maya: timeline sounds okay; the main dependency is partner pricing approval and CedarBridge security review. we'll push the security pack right after this call.

[15:40] Jonah: for the perf bake we'll need a representative dataset and a traffic profile. prefer a synthetic burst pattern that matches your peak — you indicated 18k rps peak for the analytics pipeline?
[15:52] Sarah: yes roughly 15-20k during batch windows, but sustained is lower. we'll share a csv and few sample payloads.

[18:10] Tom: security — two items: KMS integration and audit logs retention for 12 months. Any gotchas?
[18:20] Priya: northbridge has done redwood pilots before, we had to map KMS access via our key management gateway.
[18:29] Jonah: redwood supports customer-managed keys and audit log exports to s3/gs. caveat: if you use private on-prem we provide offline package but it takes ops time. for hosted we can do KMS and logging via a secure forwarder.

[21:45] Sarah: on compliance we also need SOC2 attestation docs and an architecture diagram for our risk team.
[21:52] Maya: already in flight. i'll drop the SOC2 + architecture link after this call.
[21:57] Maya: (link) Deck: https://docs.redwood.ai/cases/cedarbridge-initial-deck  — this has the draft win plan.

[25:00] Alex: on the economics — priya, what discount band are we thinking for channel co-sell?
[25:08] Priya: we usually operate at 15-20% for strategic deals, plus channel credit. but we need redwood confirmation on the discount band and whether we can offer a pilot credit.
[25:18] Maya: we can do partner banding; we typically require a minimum commitment for higher discounts. i'll propose two options in the pricing sheet: a 6-month pilot with credits and a committed 12-month reserved capacity option.

[28:40] Tom: can you give an example TCO comparison for the pilot vs reserved? we care about unit costs at 1M tokens/day.
[28:50] Jonah: yes, i'll build a simple delta table — streaming costs vs batch optimized. i'll include KV cache hit rate assumptions.

[31:05] Priya: competition — cedarbridge evaluated monolithai but they couldn't meet the regional isolation ask. cloudendpoints was cheaper but latency was higher.
[31:16] Maya: noted, i'll make sure the win plan highlights latency SLO and private deployment benefits.

[34:30] Sarah: risk — if the perf bake fails to meet 99th pct at target load, what's the fall back?
[34:38] Jonah: if we can't meet the 99th we can propose a staged rollout: push latency-sensitive routes to a higher-tier model or add reserved capacity in critical windows. we can also enable model fallback to a smaller context to reduce token compute.

[37:55] Lena: ops question — who will own the PoC sign-off criteria? we recommend a 3-block definition: 1) functional correctness 2) latency SLO at 99th at X load 3) security checklist completed. who from cedarbridge will sign?
[38:12] Sarah: i'll be product owner for functional but tom will sign for infra/security.

[40:30] Maya: excellent. let's put the sign-off owners in the joint win plan.

[43:00] Jonah: perf bake logistics — propose a 2 hr session where we run your sample traffic and capture token-level latency, token-cost, and cache hit rates. alex + i will pair-run. we need dataset by 5/21.
[43:12] Alex: i'll reach out post-call to set up secure data transfer. we'll use partner gateway SFTP or presigned s3.

[45:20] Priya: on exec path — northbridge will intro cedarbridge exec to maya for an executive briefing. we find exec buy-in accelerates procurement.
[45:30] Maya: yes, an exec briefing deck is helpful; we'll prep a 15-min exec summary.

[47:55] Sarah: any blockers on legal? we have some custom DPA requests around data retention.
[48:04] Maya: send the DPA redlines; our legal ops will triage. may need partner input where channel credits affect contract terms.

[50:20] Maya: recap — action items: maya to send deck + recording, jonah to schedule perf bake and produce TCO delta, priya to confirm discount band, sarah to share dataset and traffic profile, lena to consolidate win-plan and owners.
[50:35] Tom: sounds good. one last ask — can we spotlight a customer case with similar scale?
[50:42] Maya: yes i'll include a short case study (anonymized) and latency numbers.
[50:50] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf bake and share the pricing sheet.
[50:58] Priya: thanks all.
[51:05] Alex: thanks.
[51:10] Sarah: thanks.
[51:12] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap, some product names mistranscribed (e.g., kv cache as 'k v cache'), minor filler words removed for readability.
